You are fixing a bug in the luxon repository checked out at /luxon (JavaScript date library, version 1.20.0, tests with jest: run `cd /luxon && npx jest`). Work ONLY in /luxon. Do NOT modify any file under /luxon/test (pre-existing tests must not be edited). Do NOT look at other installed copies of luxon or the internet.

TASK: There is an injected bug in /luxon/src/duration.js. When it is fixed, a test named `Duration#normalize can convert all unit pairs` must pass. That test is NOT in the repository; its name describes the expected behaviour: `Duration#normalize()` (and the underlying conversion matrices in src/duration.js: `lowOrderMatrix`, `casualMatrix`, `accurateMatrix`, `daysInMonthAccurate`, `daysInYearAccurate`, etc.) must be able to convert between every ordered pair of units (years, quarters, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes, seconds, milliseconds) in both directions, i.e. for every pair of distinct units u1, u2: `Duration.fromObject({[u1]: 1}).as(u2)` must return a finite, positive, correct number, and normalizing a duration in one unit must produce the same instant when converted back.

Look at src/duration.js: the matrices are built with helper functions (`antiTrivial`, `reverseMatrix`, `normalizeValues`, `asNumber`, `matrixToObject`) and there is likely a subtly wrong entry, a wrong index, a swapped pair, a missing/inverted entry, or a wrong constant in one of the matrices (e.g. a value in `lowOrderMatrix`, `casualMatrix` or `accurateMatrix`, or a wrong divisor like 7 vs 24 vs 60 vs 1000, or a wrong `daysInMonthAccurate`/`daysInYearAccurate`). Compare each matrix entry against the mathematical definition of the unit conversions (1 year = 12 months = 4 quarters = 365 days (casual) / 365.2425 days (accurate); 1 week = 7 days; 1 day = 24 hours; 1 hour = 60 minutes; 1 minute = 60 seconds; 1 second = 1000 milliseconds; 1 quarter = 3 months).

Fix the bug minimally and in place. Do not add features, do not change public API, do not reformat unrelated code.

VERIFY: (a) write a temporary test OUTSIDE the test directory (e.g. /luxon/.tmpcheck_dur/x.test.js, run with `cd /luxon && npx jest --roots /luxon/.tmpcheck_dur`) that checks `Duration.fromObject({[u1]: 1}).as(u2)` for all ordered pairs of the units above (and `shiftTo`/`normalize` round trips), and delete that directory when done; (b) run the full suite `cd /luxon && npx jest` and confirm the ONLY failures are the 2 pre-existing failures in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js (they fail before your change too, locale/Intl related). If your change makes any other test fail, revert and rethink.

REPORT back: the exact file+line of the root cause, the diff you applied, the verification output (jest summary lines), and any uncertainty.

TASK: There is an injected bug in /luxon/src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js. When it is fixed, two tests must pass: `A DateTime in an invalid FixedOffsetZone is itself invalid` and `FixedOffsetZone is invalid when constructed with a non-numeric offset`. Neither is in the repository; their names describe the expected behaviour: constructing a FixedOffsetZone with a non-numeric offset (e.g. `FixedOffsetZone.instance("blorp")`, or `DateTime.local().setZone("UTC+blorp")` / `FixedOffsetZone.parseSpecifier("UTC+blorp")`) must yield an INVALID zone (`zone.isValid === false`), and any DateTime created in such a zone must itself be invalid (`dt.isValid === false`, `dt.invalidReason === "unsupported zone"`).

Look at /luxon/src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js (compare it with the other zone implementations in /luxon/src/zones/IANAZone.js and /luxon/src/zones/InvalidZone.js, and with how `normalizeZone` in /luxon/src/impl/zoneUtil.js and `DateTime#setZone` in /luxon/src/datetime.js consume zones). The likely injected bug is a missing/incorrect validity check (e.g. `isValid` getter, `instance()`/`parseSpecifier()` not validating that the offset is a number, or a wrong `isNumber`/`Number.isNaN` check).

Fix it minimally and in place: no new features, no public API changes, no unrelated reformatting.

VERIFY: (a) write a temporary test OUTSIDE the test directory (e.g. /luxon/.tmpcheck_zone/x.test.js, run with `cd /luxon && npx jest --roots /luxon/.tmpcheck_zone`) covering: `FixedOffsetZone.instance("blorp").isValid === false`, `FixedOffsetZone.instance(60).isValid === true`, `DateTime.fromObject({year:2020,month:1,day:1},{zone: FixedOffsetZone.instance("blorp")}).isValid === false`, `DateTime.local().setZone("UTC+blorp").isValid === false`, and that valid offsets still work (`DateTime.fromISO("2020-01-01T00:00:00+05:30").offset === 330`); delete that directory when done; (b) run the full suite `cd /luxon && npx jest` and confirm the ONLY failures are the 2 pre-existing failures in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js (locale/Intl related, they fail before your change too). If any other test fails, revert and rethink.

REPORT back: the exact file+line of the root cause, the diff you applied, the verification output (jest summary lines), and any uncertainty. Note: other agents are concurrently editing src/impl/util.js, src/duration.js and src/datetime.js — do NOT touch those files.

TASK: There is an injected bug in /luxon/src/datetime.js. When it is fixed, a test named `DateTime#isInDST() returns true for 1974 whole year in USA- from January 6th to October 27th` must pass. That test is NOT in the repository; its name describes the expected behaviour: in 1974 the USA observed year-round daylight saving time (Emergency Daylight Saving Time Energy Conservation Act) from January 6th 1974 to October 27th 1974, so for every date in that range, `DateTime.fromObject({year: 1974, month: M, day: D}, {zone: "America/New_York"}).isInDST` must be true (and false before Jan 6 and after Oct 27).

Evidence already gathered by me (reproduce it yourself): with `{zone: "America/New_York"}`,
- `DateTime.fromObject({year:1974,month:6,day:1},{zone:"America/New_York"}).isInDST` is true and `.set({month:1}).offset` is -300 (correct)
- but `DateTime.fromObject({year:1974,month:6,day:7},{zone:"America/New_York"}).isInDST` is FALSE, and for that date `.set({month:1}).offset` returns -240 (the summer/DST offset) instead of -300. Same wrongness for most days of the year.
So something in `DateTime#set()` / `fixOffset()` / offset handling in src/datetime.js is broken for these dates. Note `get isInDST()` in src/datetime.js compares `this.offset` with `this.set({month:1}).offset` and `this.set({month:5}).offset`.

INVESTIGATE the real root cause in src/datetime.js (compare the code with how the rest of the file uses it; look for a subtly wrong condition/argument, e.g. in `fixOffset`, `set`, `objToLocalTS` usage, or offset caching). Fix it minimally and in place. Do not add features, do not refactor unrelated code, do not change public API.

VERIFY: (a) write a temporary test OUTSIDE the test directory (e.g. /luxon/.tmpcheck_dst/x.test.js, run with `cd /luxon && npx jest --roots /luxon/.tmpcheck_dst`) that checks every day from 1974-01-01 to 1974-12-31 in America/New_York has the expected isInDST value, and delete that directory when done; (b) run the full suite `cd /luxon && npx jest` and confirm the ONLY failures are the 2 pre-existing failures in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js (they fail before your change too, they are locale/Intl related). If your change makes any other test fail, revert and rethink.

REPORT back: the exact file+line of the root cause, the diff you applied, the verification output (jest summary lines), and any uncertainty.
